paths.name: marked
paths.message: ⚠️  M-4: 'marked' produces raw HTML strings that are unsafe for dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization. In this codebase, any XSS vulnerability directly enables CSRF forgery (csrf_token is not HttpOnly — required by the double-submit pattern). If you need Markdown rendering, pipe the output through sanitizeArticleContent() before passing it to dangerouslySetInnerHTML. To suppress after a conscious review, add eslint-disable-next-line with a justification. See lib/csrf.ts.

paths.name: remark-html
paths.message: ⚠️  M-4: 'remark-html' serialises the remark AST directly to a raw HTML string. The output is unsafe for dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization. Use remark → rehype → custom serialiser with an allowlist instead, or pipe through sanitizeArticleContent(). Any XSS enables CSRF here (csrf_token is not HttpOnly). See lib/csrf.ts.

no-restricted-syntax.message: ⚠️  dangerouslyAllowSVG: true requires a mandatory security review regardless of remotePatterns. This flag allows next/image to serve SVG files, which can execute arbitrary JavaScript at the main origin if a crafted SVG reaches any image path — even if remotePatterns is currently empty. User-controlled writes to public/ (CMS syncs, CI artefacts, webhook handlers) are dangerous with this flag set, as no remote origin is needed to exploit it. To suppress this error after a conscious review, add an eslint-disable-next-line comment DIRECTLY ABOVE this line with a written justification covering: (1) why this flag is needed, (2) why it is currently safe (e.g. remotePatterns is empty AND no user-controlled content can reach any image path served by next/image), AND (3) the specific conditions that would require removing it. That justification comment will be visible in code review. See next.config.mjs for the full rationale and removal triggers.

⚠️  You have added entries to remotePatterns. Before committing, verify that dangerouslyAllowSVG is set to false (or removed) in next.config.mjs, or that SVG images are served from a sandboxed origin. Leaving dangerouslyAllowSVG: true with non-empty remotePatterns enables stored-XSS via crafted SVG payloads from remote sources.

⚠️  dangerouslySetInnerHTML requires a security review before merging. In this codebase, any XSS vulnerability directly enables CSRF forgery because csrf_token is not HttpOnly (required by the double-submit cookie pattern). Only two uses are pre-approved without review: (1) { __html: safeJsonLd(…) } for JSON-LD script blocks, and (2) { __html: safeContent } for article body HTML that has been run through sanitizeArticleContent(). Any other use — Markdown renderer output, CMS snippets, rich-text editor HTML, raw template strings — must be sanitized through sanitizeArticleContent() or sanitizeText() first. To suppress this error after a conscious review, add an eslint-disable-next-line comment that explains what prevents XSS in this specific case. That comment will be visible in code review. See lib/csrf.ts for the full XSS→CSRF escalation analysis.

⚠️  DB-1: Raw $regex with a user-supplied string is a ReDoS and NoSQL injection vector. A pattern like `.*.*.*.*` causes catastrophic backtracking that can hang the Node.js event loop for seconds; at 200 concurrent requests the site becomes unresponsive. Instead, use MongoDB $text search with the article_text_search index (already created by scripts/create-indexes.ts): { $text: { $search: query } }. If $regex is unavoidable for a specific case, you MUST: (1) wrap the value in escapeSearchQuery() from lib/articles.ts to escape all PCRE metacharacters, AND (2) enforce the MAX_QUERY_LENGTH cap (also from lib/articles.ts) before passing the string to the query. To suppress this error after applying both safeguards, add an eslint-disable-next-line comment explaining why $text search is unsuitable here and confirming escapeSearchQuery + MAX_QUERY_LENGTH are applied.

⚠️  M-1: COOKIE-PRIVILEGE-CHECK — cookies.set() for rl_search uses sameSite: 'lax', which is safe only while the cookie carries no session state or privilege-granting data. If you are changing this cookie to store session state or grant any form of access, you MUST: (1) change sameSite to 'strict', (2) update the COOKIE-PRIVILEGE-CHECK sentinel comment directly above this call to describe the new privilege model, and (3) add an eslint-disable-next-line comment here with a written justification. See middleware.ts (enforceSearchRateLimit) for the full rationale.

rules: Resolution: CSP is no longer request-specific

no-restricted-syntax.message: ⚠️  cookies() in a Server Component or shared component renders cookie-personalised HTML. Several routes that render through this component are now statically generated or served via ISR (see middleware.ts 'Resolution: CSP is no longer request-specific' and the per-route `revalidate` exports), so a cached response containing this personalisation would be served to every other visitor who hits the same cached path — not just a theoretical risk if some CDN override ever caches it. Fix: (a) make the route render dynamically and confirm no CDN override caches it anyway, OR (b) move per-user state to a Client Component. Add eslint-disable-next-line with a comment confirming your chosen fix. See .eslintrc.json (M-2) for the full analysis.

⚠️  cookies() called inside app/category/**. This route receives Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=3600 from next.config.mjs (D-2 fix) — it is genuinely edge-cached today, not just a theoretical CDN-override risk. If any Server Component reads a cookie to alter the HTML, the personalised response would be cached and replayed to every other visitor who hits the same path. Fix: either (a) remove the /category/:slug Cache-Control rule in next.config.mjs and confirm no other CDN override forces caching anyway, or (b) move the per-user state to a Client Component resolved after hydration. Add an eslint-disable-next-line comment confirming which option you chose. See .eslintrc.json (H-4) for the full analysis.
